name: [dev] Worker job failing repeatedly — ticks caught, host alive
message:
## What's happening

One or more `CardiTrack.Worker` jobs threw on their scheduled tick. `CronBackgroundService` caught the exception, logged it, and left the host running — so the process is healthy but that job is **not doing its work**.

## Why it matters

This is the quiet failure mode. Before the tick guard existed, a throwing job took the whole host down, which was catastrophic but at least obvious. Now the host survives, which means a job can fail silently on every tick indefinitely. This monitor is what replaces the crash as the signal.

Depending on which job it is, the silent damage differs: missed escalations mean an alert never reaches a carer; missed wearable sync means stale readings feeding baselines; missed partition maintenance eventually means write failures.

## First steps

1. `service:worker "Scheduled invocation of"` in Logs — the message names the job (`Scheduled invocation of {Job} failed`).
2. Read `@exception.stacktrace` on the same log line for the cause.
3. Check whether it is failing *every* tick or intermittently. Every tick usually means config/DI/permissions; intermittent usually means a dependency (Cloud SQL, Fitbit/Google API, FCM) is flaking.

NOTE: threshold is 3 in 15 minutes, which trips quickly for fast-cadence jobs (30s–5m) but takes longer for hourly ones. Tune per-job if that proves too slow.

NOTE: no notification handle is attached yet. Add one (e.g. `@slack-...`) to make this page someone.
